name: Keeper of the Plains
unique: A 44 foot steel sculpture of a Native American figure at the confluence of two rivers, with a fire ring lit at dusk and a bridge over the water.
buzz: The sculpture is striking and the sunset fire is the moment. Free and quick.

name: Sedgwick County Zoo
unique: A 247 acre zoo with elephants, gorillas, a farm, a train and a children's petting area, one of the best in the Plains.
buzz: Big enough for a full day and shady in stretches. The train is the kid favorite.

name: Exploration Place
unique: A hands on science center on the Arkansas River with a design studio, a flight simulator and a dome theater.
buzz: Good for a rainy day, with enough for kids of different ages. The river setting is nice.

name: Massachusetts Street
unique: A wide main street of independent shops, bars and restaurants beside the university, with a history of free state politics.
buzz: The street is walkable and busy on weekends. The burger joints and bookshops are the local institutions.

name: KU Natural History Museum
unique: A university museum with dinosaur fossils, a giant mosasaur, Kansas fossils and a live beehive.
buzz: Free and genuinely good, especially the mosasaur. A quick stop for kids.

name: Strataca
unique: A tour 650 feet underground in a working salt mine, with tunnels, mining equipment and a underground vault.
buzz: The descent and the scale of the mine are the experience. Bring a jacket, it is cool down there.

name: Brown v. Board of Education National Historical Park
unique: A museum in the Monroe Elementary School, one of the segregated schools in the case, with the story of the five lawsuits that ended school segregation.
buzz: The school itself is the exhibit and the ranger talks are excellent. Free.

name: Kansas State Capitol
unique: A copper domed capitol with a mural by John Steuart Curry, a legislative chamber and a dome tour to the top.
buzz: The Curry mural and the dome climb are the reasons. Free, with tours on the hour.

name: Little Sweden
unique: A Swedish heritage town with a main street of Dala horses, a folk art center, a college and a annual Svensk Hyllningsfest.
buzz: The Dala horses are everywhere and the town is charming. The Swedish pancakes are the lunch.

name: Old Market
unique: A warehouse district of cobblestone streets, brick buildings, galleries and restaurants, with horse drawn carriages and buskers.
buzz: The streets are photogenic and the food is good. Busy on weekend evenings.

name: Joslyn Art Museum
unique: A free museum in a Art Deco building with European and American art, Native American works and a sculpture garden.
buzz: Free and strong, with a beautiful building and a good cafe. The Western art collection is the local specialty.

name: The Durham Museum
unique: A museum in the Art Deco Union Station, with trains, a soda fountain, a street of old storefronts and the history of the Union Pacific.
buzz: The station itself is gorgeous and the trains are the kid draw. Allow two hours.

name: Lauritzen Gardens
unique: A 100 acre botanical garden with a conservatory, a model train garden, a rose garden and a woodland trail.
buzz: The model trains are the kid hit and the conservatory is the winter escape. Good in every season.

name: Sheldon Museum of Art
unique: A free university art museum in a Philip Johnson building, with American art, modernism and a sculpture garden.
buzz: The building is the draw and the collection is free. Quiet on weekdays.

name: Nebraska State Capitol
unique: A 400 foot tower with a Nebraska life mural, a unicameral chamber and an observation deck with a view of the plains.
buzz: The building is one of the best state capitols, and the dome tour is worth it. Free.

name: Ashfall Fossil Beds
unique: A fossil bed where a volcanic ash fall killed a herd of rhinos, horses and camels 12 million years ago, now exposed in a working quarry.
buzz: The skeletons are still in the ground where they died, which is the fascinating part. Seasonal, so check dates.

name: Niobrara River
unique: A spring fed river through the Sandhills with waterfalls, pine bluffs and a gentle current, one of the best floats in the Plains.
buzz: The water is clear and the trip is easy. Rent a tube or a canoe and go in summer.

name: Scotts Bluff National Monument
unique: A bluff that guided Oregon Trail wagons, with a summit road, trails and a museum of the westward migration.
buzz: The summit drive has the view and the trail is short. The Oregon Trail ruts are nearby.

name: Philbrook Museum of Art
unique: A 1920s Italianate villa turned art museum, with a strong Native American collection and formal gardens.
buzz: The house and the gardens are as good as the art, and the Native American collection is excellent.

name: Woody Guthrie Center
unique: A museum of the folk singer's life, with his lyrics, drawings, guitars and the archive of his recordings.
buzz: The archive is serious and the story is moving. Good for anyone interested in American music.

name: Cain's Ballroom
unique: A 1924 dance hall where Bob Wills and the Texas Playboys broadcast, still booking rock, country and indie acts under the original sign.
buzz: The room is legendary and the sound is good. Check the calendar and buy ahead.

name: National Cowboy and Western Heritage Museum
unique: A museum of the American West with Western paintings, saddles, firearms, a reconstructed town and the End of the Trail sculpture.
buzz: Bigger and better than expected, with serious art alongside the cowboy gear. Allow two hours.

name: Bricktown
unique: A warehouse district of brick buildings, restaurants, a canal with water taxis and a ballpark, next to downtown.
buzz: The canal walk is the thing to do and the food is decent. Busy on weekends.

name: Myriad Botanical Gardens
unique: A 17 acre downtown garden with a glass conservatory, a children's garden, a lake and an ice rink in winter.
buzz: The conservatory is the rainy day win and the outdoor gardens are free. Good for kids.

name: Price Tower
unique: Frank Lloyd Wright's only built skyscraper, a 19 story copper and concrete tower with tours and a small hotel.
buzz: For architecture people it is a pilgrimage, and the tour explains the design. The top floor view is a bonus.

name: Medicine Park
unique: A cobblestone resort town at the edge of the Wichita Mountains, with a creek, a swimming hole, cabins and a dam built of river rock.
buzz: The cobblestone buildings are charming and the creek is cool. Good base for the wildlife refuge.
